summary_en: This phase 2a pilot trial tests riluzole against a placebo to see how it affects circulating BDNF levels in people with cancer-related cognitive impairment. The study includes people with many cancer types, including breast cancer, sarcoma, gastric cancer, lung cancer, head and neck cancer, and colorectal cancer. Participants take riluzole 50 mg by mouth twice daily (every 12 hours) for 8 weeks, or a matching placebo capsule on the same schedule. The study measures the effect on circulating BDNF levels, which is the main outcome stated.
summary_es: Este ensayo piloto de fase 2a compara riluzol con un placebo para observar cómo afecta los niveles circulantes de BDNF en personas con deterioro cognitivo relacionado con el cáncer. El estudio incluye personas con varios tipos de cáncer, entre ellos cáncer de mama, sarcoma, cáncer gástrico, cáncer de pulmón, cáncer de cabeza y cuello, y cáncer colorrectal. Los participantes toman riluzol de 50 mg por vía oral dos veces al día (cada 12 horas) durante 8 semanas, o una cápsula de placebo con el mismo horario. El estudio mide el efecto sobre los niveles circulantes de BDNF, que es el resultado principal indicado.
who_for: Adults 18 or older who feel cognition has worsened since cancer treatment or brain radiation.
Cohort A: breast cancer treatment, or non-breast cancer with anthracycline, platinum, or other anticancer therapy in the past 3 years, and no prior brain radiat
Cohort B: prior radiotherapy or radiosurgery to the brain, with life expectancy over 6 months.
Able to give informed consent and complete questionnaires and computer tests in English, Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese, or Spanish.
not_for: Primary brain tumors or brain metastases (Cohort A), or high grade glioma (Cohort B).
Unwilling to complete the neuropsychological assessments needed for the study.
Pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study.
Suspected hypersensitivity to riluzole, current smoking, cannabis use, or taking listed interacting medicines.
AST or ALT at least 3 times the upper limit of normal, or serious conditions the investigator judges would preclude participation.
